title: Grain Desk Standing Rule: Which Tickets an Amendment Credits, and at What
content:
Which tickets are credited on an amendment under Grain Marketing Contracts, and at what, turns on where they were received; every ticket standing against the contract counts here, whatever the disposition.

**1.** Where two or more tickets stand against the contract and every one of them was received at the facility the contract calls for, all of them are credited at the net bushels written on them.

**2.** Where tickets stand that were received at another facility, the tickets received at the facility the contract calls for are credited at their net bushels and the others at their net bushels less the off-facility allowance of 0.75 percent.

**3.** Where neither of those holds, only the tickets received at the facility the contract calls for are credited.

## The three cases in one view

| Tickets standing against the contract, whatever the disposition | Received elsewhere | Credited |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | none | all of them, at the net bushels written on them |
| any number | at least one | the contracted-facility tickets at their net bushels, the others at their net bushels less 0.75 percent |
| 1 | none | that ticket, being received at the contracted facility |
| 0 | none | nothing |

## Illustration on hypothetical tickets

Four tickets stand against a contract, three received at the facility the contract calls for carrying 9,000 net bushels between them and one received elsewhere carrying 3,000. The credit is 9,000 bushels plus 3,000 less 0.75 percent, being 2,977.50, so 11,977.50 bushels are credited. Had all four been received at the contracted facility, carrying 12,000 net bushels between them, all 12,000 would be credited.
